name: Old Crow Medicine Show
sources: style-research-extended-2 vol.2 country-train — Old Crow Medicine Show
notes: Old-time Appalachian string band played with punk energy — the pre-bluegrass wing of the archetype, where the subdivision comes from clawhammer banjo and fiddle rather than Scruggs rolls. The source describes them as "a bluegrass-powered locomotive", which the entry notes is the archetype's own name in prose. The drum block is where this model separates from the rest of the wing, and it is stated as an instruction: "the backbeat by guitar down-strokes and by the whole band's hand-claps and stomps, which are a documented feature of the sound rather than an overdub. Model group percussion (claps, stomps, washboard) as a first-class backbeat layer in this entry." So `percs` is the loudest in the bluegrass wing by a wide margin — snap, woodblock, tambourine and rim at [2,5] per bar and only −2 dB — where every neighbour here sits at −9 to −13. The punk energy is the humanize block: `quantizeStrength` 0.78 with 7–9 ms of jitter and 0.22 velocity variance, the loosest setting in this section, against the tight bluegrass norm beside it. The upright is the other stated backbeat: "root–five two-beat with slap accents used aggressively — the slap is the snare in this band", hence `followRootsProb` 0.94 with the narrowest passing-tone set of the wing. Harmony is deliberately plain and the entry says so — "three chords, 4- or 8-bar loops, no chromatic motion" — so `extensions.triad` is 0.9, the highest in this section, with I–IV–V at weight 6 and a twelve-bar frame for the blues numbers. Vocals are "shouted group unison as often as they are harmonised, and the harmony is rougher and wider than the bluegrass stack", which is the staccato articulation and the octave_echo share in the countermelody. ⚠ INFERRED: `bpm.mode` 150 (the entry states 100–200 and says "tempo band inferred [LOW-CONF]"), the velocity tiers, the −4 ms offset and every melody, countermelody and bassline number. ⚠ The documented tempo-accelerando habit — "the final chorus with the whole band shouting in unison and the tempo pushing forward", which the entry says is in-grammar here and nowhere else in the section — has no field in this schema and is recorded rather than encoded.
